nodes.name: Electrolyte Preparation
nodes.procedure: A 30 wt. % KOH electrolyte was prepared using KOH pellets and water. To dope the electrolyte, specific amounts (12.5, 25, or 250 μM) of Fe2(SO4)3 hydrate were added to reach targeted Fe concentrations. For low concentrations, stirring and ultrasonication were used to dissolve the resulting Fe(OH)3 precipitate.

nodes.name: Cathodic Electrochemical Conditioning
nodes.procedure: The cleaned Ni-201 electrode was conditioned in the Fe-doped KOH electrolyte at a current density of -400 mA/cm2 for 1 to 2.5 hours. This results in the formation of metallic Fe dendrites due to reduction from electrolyte Fe.

unit_operations.name: Galvanostatic Pretreatment
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: pretreatment was conducted, where the current density was set to 400 mA/cm2 ... for 1.0 to 2.5 h

nodes.name: Anodic Electrochemical Conditioning
nodes.procedure: The cleaned Ni-201 electrode was conditioned in the Fe-doped KOH electrolyte at a current density of +400 mA/cm2 for 1 to 2.5 hours. This facilitates the in-situ formation of mixed Ni/Fe oxyhydroxide species.

nodes.description: HER performance evaluation in a three-electrode cell with varying electrolyte Fe concentrations
nodes.source_text: Three-electrode cell experiments show that Fe ([Fe] = 6–357 μM; ICP-OES) promotes HER... lowering both overpotentials by at least 100 mV... The HER values for the Tafel slope are similar to values expected from literature... At 35.4 C and 54.7 C we can observe that for both HER and OER the capacitance at least doubles when increasing the Fe concentration from 6 to 357 μM.

nodes.description: OER performance evaluation in a three-electrode cell with varying electrolyte Fe concentrations
nodes.source_text: For the OER we can observe a significant drop in IR-corrected half-cell potential with increasing Fe concentration at all temperatures surmounting to as much as 200 mV... OER probably benefits from the formation of thin layers of mixed Ni/Fe oxyhydroxides.

nodes.description: Performance evaluation in a zero-gap flow cell with varying electrolyte Fe concentrations
nodes.source_text: The overpotential of a zero-gap flow cell was decreased by 200 mV when increasing the Fe concentration... performance gain of 20%... At 549 μM the surface deposited Fe reaches at least up to 1.85 μm in thickness.

nodes.characterization_summary: Identified NiH_x or Ni(OH)2 formation (0.27-0.33 V/RHE) and NiO(OH) oxidation (1.30-1.42 V/RHE). Higher Fe concentrations introduced Fe reduction/oxidation peaks between -0.2 and +0.6 V/RHE.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The first CV obtained at 35 C shows a broad peak with a maximum located between 0.27 and 0.33 V/RHE ... at higher potentials between 1.30 and 1.42 V/RHE the Ni2+ species are further oxidized to form NiO(OH).

nodes.characterization_summary: Double-layer capacitance (proportional to ECSA) at least doubles when Fe concentration increases to 357 μM; HER capacitance is higher than OER capacitance due to Fe deposition.
nodes.evidence_snippet: At 35 C and 55 C we can observe that for both HER and OER the capacitance at least doubles when increasing the Fe concentration ... indicating that Fe deposition increases the surface area.

nodes.characterization_summary: Morphological analysis shows the formation of dendritic, needle-like Fe crystals (~μm in size) on the cathode, while the anode surface shows no such structural changes.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Fe particles that form on the cathode surface have a dendritic shape, forming black needle-like crystals, a few μm in size ... On the anode’s surface no indication of Fe deposition was observed

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS identified metallic Fe(0) at 705.6 eV on the cathode. Depth profiling determined the deposited Fe layer thickness exceeds 1.85 μm at high electrolyte Fe concentrations (549 μM). Overlap with Ni LMM lines hindered definitive FeOOH assignment.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution XPS spectra exhibit the main Fe 2p 3/2 peak at 705.6 eV, which is an indication of the presence of Fe(0) ... at 549 μM the surface deposited Fe reaches at least up to 1.85 μm in thickness

nodes.characterization_summary: Surface elemental analysis confirms that the Fe/Ni ratio on the cathode increases with electrolyte Fe concentration due to deposition, whereas the anode surface composition remains relatively invariant.
nodes.evidence_snippet: When the working electrode was employed for HER, an increasing Fe to Ni ratio can be observed with an increasing electrolyte Fe concentration. ... when the working electrode is employed for OER, we can see that the surface Fe to Ni ratio is rather invariant

nodes.characterization_summary: Visual inspection of the electrodes post-electrolysis reveals the growth of dark-colored dendrite structures on the cathode surface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Optical and SEM images of electrodes post electrolysis ... Optical image of cathode ... post-electrolysis with 55 μM of electrolyte Fe showing ... dendrite structures
